intro: An AI assistant for business analysts on Mac answers questions about the screen in front of you. Lazur does that by voice. Hold ⌥⌘, ask out loud, and Lazur answers and points at what you need. This guide covers where analyst time goes, what a realistic day looks like, and where voice help saves steps in Excel, Word and Slack.
tldr: Analysts lose time to searching for answers, constant interruptions and rewriting the same documents.
Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and it answers out loud.
It explains formulas, points at menus, guides you one click at a time and drafts text. It does not click or edit for you.
Your employer's rules on customer and financial data still decide what you can show an AI tool.

blocks.text: Where a business analyst's day really goes

Your job title says analysis. Your day often says search, reply and rewrite. Atlassian's State of Teams 2025 report says leaders and teams waste 25% of their time searching for answers. The report comes from a survey of 12,000 knowledge workers and 200 executives. It gives a share of time, not an hours figure, so read it as a share.

Interruptions add to the search. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index says workers are interrupted every 2 minutes in the 9-to-5 day. The same report says 60% of meetings are ad hoc rather than scheduled. The call you blocked out is often not the call you end up in. Your spec time gets cut into small pieces.

Business analysts have no category of their own in the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. The closest page covers management analysts. It lists 1,077,100 jobs in 2025 and projects 10% growth from 2025 to 2035. Use those figures as context for a close relative of your job, not as a measure of your week. The page says management analysts gather information, interview personnel and analyze financial and other data. It also says many write proposals when they bid for contract work. That matches the work most analysts describe. It is still a proxy.
Excel help: a voice assistant for the numbers

Excel is where analysts test whether a story holds. A lookup that quietly returns N/A can change a forecast. A filter left on in a PivotTable can hide a whole region. Voice help is useful here because your hands stay on the keyboard while you ask the question.

Lazur does not run inside Excel. It is not a plugin or add-in, and it does not edit your workbook. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about what is on screen. Lazur answers out loud, circles the thing you ask about, or walks you through the steps while you do them.

Excel for Mac 16.114.3 (build 26102720) came out on October 27, 2026. Microsoft's release notes for that build list quality and performance fixes, and no Excel feature or menu change. The menus you learned still apply. To check your version, go to Excel > About Microsoft Excel.

blocks.text: Ask for the path, not only the answer. When you ask why a formula fails, Lazur reads the formula bar and the cells the formula points at. Then check the source sheet yourself. A voice answer is a lead, not proof.

For a walkthrough, ask for a guide. Lazur guides you one click at a time, and it waits for each click before it moves on. That is slower than a video. It keeps you in your own file, with your own data, in front of you.
Word for specs and proposals: an AI assistant for Word on Mac

Word is where analysts write requirements, proposals and change summaries. Much of the time goes to rewording and to checking what changed since last time. Two Word features help with that work. Track Changes records each edit. Compare shows the difference between two files.

To turn on Track Changes, go to Review > Track Changes, or press ⌘⇧E. To compare two versions, go to Review > Compare. The full steps are in our guide to [comparing two documents in Word](/how-to/compare-two-documents-in-word).

Dictation helps with the first draft. Hold fn and speak. The text lands at the cursor in the app you are using, with capitals and punctuation. Add product names and acronyms to your personal dictionary so they come out right. Save the paragraph you paste into every spec as a snippet.

blocks.title: Turn boilerplate into a snippet
blocks.text: If you paste the same assumptions block into every spec, make it a snippet. Dictate it once, then reuse it by name. The wording stays the same across documents, and you stop retyping it.

Use Lazur for word choice, not for the decision. Ask it to explain a sentence a stakeholder misread. Ask for three ways to say the same rule. Pick one, then check it against your source notes. The rule itself still needs your sign-off.
Slack and email: keeping decisions out of the thread

Analysts spend much of the day in chat and email. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index says chats sent outside the 9-to-5 day rose 15% year over year. It averages 58 messages per user before or after hours. The decision you need is often in one of those threads. Lazur can read what is on screen and help you find it.

In Slack, press ⌘K to jump to a channel or a person. If a project thread keeps growing, create a channel for it. Public and private channels work differently. Our guide to [creating a channel in Slack](/how-to/create-a-channel-in-slack) covers the choice.

If you still use Legacy Outlook for Mac, you cannot add or remove ribbon buttons. You also cannot change the button size. Microsoft's support page says you can show or hide the ribbon with View > Ribbon. That page has no publication date, so check it against your own version before you rely on it.

blocks.text: Record the outcome of each decision in the spec. Include the date and the person who made the call. A decision left in a Slack thread gets lost, and the next analyst has to search for it again.
Research for vendors and comparisons

Analysts often compare vendors, tools and regulations. Lazur can run research in its own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. The job comes back with a summary and a report. You can keep working in your own app while it runs.

Treat research as a starting point. Use a company's own site for facts about that company. Check their pricing page directly if you are not sure what it says. Quote a number only after you have opened the page that holds it, and note the date you read it.
If a vendor page does not show a price or a feature, leave it out of the spec. A blank cell is better than a guess that ends up in a contract review.
Privacy, client data and your employer's rules

Business analysts often see customer records, payroll data and unreleased financials. Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

blocks.title: Employer rules come first
blocks.text: Follow your company's rules on customer, employee and financial data before you use any AI tool on a screen that shows that data. Lazur does not set those rules for you. Ask your manager or IT team when you are unsure.

Close sensitive files before you hold the shortcut. A screenshot shows what is on screen, so keep the payroll file closed when you ask about a spec. Lazur also keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on your Mac. Think about that when you work with restricted material.
Mistakes business analysts make with AI tools

items: Trusting a formula you have not read. Ask Lazur to explain it, then test it on rows you already know.
Asking for the answer and skipping the reasoning. Ask why a number moved, then check the source sheet.
Quoting a blog for a vendor price. Go to the vendor's own pricing page instead.
Dictating a requirement and skipping the read-through. Dictation can mishear a name, a date or a threshold.
Sending a draft you have not read through. Fluent text can still get a threshold or a name wrong.

blocks.text: Setting up Lazur for your first week

Start with the shortcut. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask a question about something on screen. Then try fn for dictation in a plain text field. Ask for a guided walkthrough once, in a file you know well, so you can judge how it works.

Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and on Intel. A Windows version is planned, but it is not available. The trial starts when you first open the app, and it does not need a credit card. Start small: one formula check, one draft and one search. Then decide where it earns its place in your day. Plans are on the [pricing page](/pricing), and you can [download Lazur](/download) for your Mac.

faq.question: What is an AI assistant for business analysts on Mac?
faq.answer: It is a tool that answers questions about the screen in front of you and helps with text, by voice. Lazur is one example. You hold ⌥⌘, ask a question, and Lazur answers out loud and points at what you need. It is not a plugin for Excel or Word.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Excel or Word?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not an add-in and does not edit your files. It looks at the screen while you hold the shortcut. Then it explains, points, guides or drafts text, and you place the result yourself.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. In guide mode, Lazur tells you where to click and waits for each click. It does not operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and on Intel. A Windows version is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: Is my data used to train AI models?
faq.answer: Content is never used to train AI models. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Check your employer's rules before you use any AI tool with customer or employee data.

faq.question: How do I use dictation for requirements?
faq.answer: Hold fn in any text field. Dictation writes clean text at the cursor. Check names, thresholds and dates after each dictation, because a misheard number can change a rule.

faq.question: Are there numbers on how much time analysts lose?
faq.answer: Not for business analysts specifically. Atlassian says leaders and teams waste 25% of their time searching for answers. Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index says workers are interrupted every 2 minutes in the 9-to-5 day. Those are general knowledge worker figures.

faq.question: Where can I see plans and prices?
faq.answer: Check the [pricing page](/pricing). The trial starts when you first open the app, and it does not need a credit card. Compare the plans against how often you would use voice help each week.

painPoints.title: Searching for answers
painPoints.text: Atlassian says leaders and teams waste 25% of their time searching for answers. For an analyst, that search runs through spreadsheets, old specs, chat threads and the company wiki.

painPoints.title: Constant interruptions
painPoints.text: Microsoft's 2025 Work Trend Index says workers are interrupted every 2 minutes in the 9-to-5 day. Each interruption breaks the thread of the spec you were writing.

painPoints.title: Meetings nobody scheduled
painPoints.text: 60% of meetings are ad hoc, according to the same Microsoft report. You get pulled into a call, then owe the team a clear summary of what was decided.

painPoints.title: Writing for other people
painPoints.text: The BLS says management analysts make recommendations through presentations or written reports, and many write proposals. That writing often comes after the real analysis, and it is the part people rush.

painPoints.title: Data checks under time pressure
painPoints.text: Most analysis lives in Excel, where one broken lookup can change the answer. Checking every formula by hand takes time you do not have before a review.

demo.spoken: Why is F14 showing N/A when this customer is in the list?
demo.result: Lazur reads the formula and the cells it points at, names the likely cause, and points at F14 with a label while it answers.
demo.context: Excel for Mac, a customer table. Column F holds a VLOOKUP, and half the rows show #N/A.
demo.output: Likely cause: the customer IDs in column B have a trailing space, so they never match column A. Try =VLOOKUP(TRIM(B14), Customers!A:C, 2, FALSE), then fill the formula down. Check one row you know first.
